description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data samples across five distinct categories used in the evaluation of large language models as cross-lingual knowledge aggregators, as referenced in the paper “1+12 Can Large Language Models Serve as Cross-Lingual Knowledge Aggregators.” The largest segment, colored red, represents “TriviaQA” and accounts for 46% of the total (1,829 samples). The second largest, in green, is “HalluEval” at 18% (721 samples). A purple segment labeled “25% (997)” — likely representing a general or baseline category — constitutes 25% of the dataset. The “Chinese Domain” is shown in yellow, making up 6% (231 samples), while “HalluQA,” in light blue, comprises 5% (185 samples). The chart uses a 3D effect with one slice (TriviaQA) slightly exploded for emphasis, and each segment is labeled with both percentage and absolute count. A small gray legend box in the upper right corner indicates the “25% (997)” category, though its label is not explicitly named in the chart itself. The segments are arranged in descending order of size clockwise from the top.
